title: Marrying Irene Armstrong and her song 'Some Other Spring'
summary: Wilson recounts meeting and marrying Irene in Chicago, her little band on Cottage Grove, her song which he recorded in 1939, and their later separation.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And I guess I should mention that I got married in Chicago at that time to Irene Armstrong, who had been married to Joe Edqy. Joe Edqy was operating, or the manager of the El Dorado Club on the southside.
Is that so? I didn't know that.
Irene Edqy, I always knew Irene, Your wife was Irene Edqy.
Yeah, she had been married to Joe Edqy, but her maiden name was Armstrong. Her roots were in Muncie, Indiana.
Oh. A very talented lady.
Yes, oh yes. She was. Irene had a little band over on Cottage Grove, I forget the name of that little club, and Big Sid was her drummer at one *The Cottage Cafe
time, and she had an excellent saxophone player, I can't remember his name, and Earl Hines' old girlfriend, Katherine Perry --
Katherine Perry! The singer.

Right, she sang and played violin with Irene's little quintet, and they made a lot of music. That's how -- I used to go over there and Irene would let me sit in her band, and when I wasn't working at the Gold Coast job, when it folded, and I could keep in practice, and that's how we got together and started going around together and finally got married.
Got married in Chicago, right?
Yes, in Chicago.
Oh, that's marvelous.

Well, I know Irene was in Chicago and I remember you were married to her, which was like to the whole music world, it was like a marriage of two great people, two talented people. She wrote a couple of songs that were very popular, didn't she?
Yes, she had a wonderful song called 'Some Other Spring.'
'Some Other Spring,' da da da da ..
Yeah, uh huh.
And you did that one, too.
Yeah, I recorded that when I had my big band in 1939.
That's right.
The vocal was sung by Jean Eldridge who was one of my favorite singers in those days.
Uh huh.
And Carmen McRae recorded it, Billie Holiday recorded it, and many instrumentalists have done it.
Is Irene still around?
No, Irene passed away recently, in the last -- I think it was this past year, in '79.
Is that so?

See, we broke up -- Irene and I separated in the middle thirties, and she remarried a man named Kitchens in Cleveland, and stayed together, as far as I know, all through the years, and she just passed away recently, in the past year.
Oh, that's too bad.
But Irene and I never had any children.
Yeah, I remember that.
